what_happened: The research report was directly plannable: its root-cause claims, the 11-for-11 retry_after:15 measurement, and the single-shot-curl-stub gap all re-verified against live files with no correction needed, so the plan spent its effort on sequencing and the two decisions research deliberately left open (constant style, testability mechanism) rather than re-deriving facts.

Research did not surface that the harness's existing 503 case would, under the new retry code, perform a real 15s sleep and still pass -- a silently slow suite rather than a red one. This forced the plan to sequence the additive stub extension (including a PATH-shadowed sleep stub) as phase 1, before the production change, so no phase ever observes an artificially slow suite.

A self-authored plan-checklist-annotation helper script used a bare '---' substring search to bound Phase 2's section, which matched a literal '# --- Constants ---' string inside one task item and briefly mis-spliced that line. Caught before committing by reading the rendered section; fixed by re-deriving the boundary from the next '\n---\n' horizontal-rule line instead. No production code affected.

Phase 4's own declared scoped check (verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4) fails Gate 3 (doc-lint) with exactly three sapience findings: deployed-content drift for sapience-retrieve.sh and test-sapience-capture.sh (source-store edits from phases 2-3, not yet redeployed) and an index-entries.json line_count mismatch for per-repo-scoping.md (self-healing: generate-context-line-counts.sh runs automatically inside deploy-headless.sh, and that script itself refuses to run pre-deploy with a clear error). All three are structurally expected given the plan's own phase ordering (content phases 1-4 precede the Phase 5 redeploy) and are not evidence of a content defect. Diff read-through independently confirms the documentation content itself is correct (no task-number references, no record-versioning language, the stale never-retries clause removed). Proceeding to Phase 5's redeploy and will re-run Gate 3 afterward to confirm it clears; will revisit Phase 4 if it does not.

Post-redeploy, the Phase 4 deferred Gate-3 doc-lint drift resolved exactly as predicted: 'bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4' now reports PASS clean for the sapience extension, and the four-suite scoped run-all.sh narrowing (test-orchestrate-build-aux-dispatch.sh, test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh, test-orchestrate-context-growth.sh, test-sapience-capture.sh) passes against the real deployed sapience-retrieve.sh with zero failures. A diff between all three source-store files and their deployed mirrors shows byte-identical content, zero drift. Per this dispatch's Batch Gate Deferral directive, Phase 5 (final phase, declared tier 'full') discharges against this scoped narrowing rather than an independent complete-gate-set run. A supplementary unflagged full 'verify-deploy.sh' run was also executed for direct observation; it showed 4 failures (gate8's 5 EXPECTED, already-baselined run-all.sh suite failures -- NOT test-sapience-capture.sh, which passed; a gate10 60s timeout; an orchestrator eager-load-budget overage; and a skill-orchestrate.md size-ceiling overage) -- none touching sapience files or this task's file_scope, confirming no regression from this task's work.
